title: paged KV-cache: block allocator reuse + locality-aware pinning optimizations
author: Liam Chen
description: Motivation: reduce GC/alloc churn and improve KV-cache hit stability under high-concurrency streaming workloads. This PR implements allocator reuse across block lifetimes and a locality-aware pinning heuristic to keep hot blocks resident on the same device/NUMA region. Changes are focused on the paged KV cache block manager: 1) introduce a small lock-free pool of recently freed blocks to avoid allocator system calls on reallocation, 2) add locality tags to blocks and prefer reusing blocks that match the request's device affinity, 3) adjust pin TTL heuristics to make short-lived pins cheaper and extend pins for blocks with high recent hit rates, 4) move critical hot-path bookkeeping out of the global mutex and into per-shard atomics to reduce contention, 5) add a simple eviction probation window to avoid thrashing when working sets temporarily exceed capacity. Benchmarks: microbench (kvcache_read_hot): - p50 latency down 12%, p95 down 18% under 128 concurrent streams; throughput improved +9% in continuous-batching scenarios with mixed sequence lengths. Memory churn reduced ~35% measured by allocator calls/sec. Backwards-compatible: no external API changes. Rollout plan: staged on Dedicated and Hosted with canary traffic; feature gated behind runtime flag kv_cache_locality_pinning. See linked Linear tasks for rollout and monitoring steps.
commits: Add block reuse pool and allocator reuse path
Attach device/numa locality tags to blocks
Optimize pin TTL heuristics and add hit-rate extension
Move per-shard bookkeeping to atomics and reduce global lock scope
Add eviction probation window and tests
Add unit/integration tests and microbench harness updates
review_comments: Sofia: Nice end-to-end. Can we avoid a global vector scan in the fallback path? Suggest adding an early exit when per-shard pool has available blocks.
Liam: Addressed by moving reuse pool to per-shard ring buffer and added early-exit logic. PTAL.
Diego: The pin TTL extension looks good but we should add a safeguard to avoid unbounded pin growth for pathological workloads.
Liam: Added max_pin_extension configuration and associated unit tests.
Asha: Integration tests showed a flaky evict_reclaim test; I tightened timing and made the probation window deterministic in tests. Verified locally.
Sofia: Approved after changes. Diego: Approved. Asha: Approved.
release_notes: Paged KV-cache: reduce allocator churn and improve cache locality under high concurrency. Expect lower tail latency and reduced memory allocation overhead; feature behind kv_cache_locality_pinning flag.
